ety.text: Attested since the 17th century. Borrowed from a Turkic source. Ultimately, from Proto-Turkic *tuman (“mist, fog”), or from Avestan 𐬛𐬎𐬥𐬨𐬀𐬥 (dunman, “fog, mist”), 𐬛𐬎𐬎𐬄𐬥𐬨𐬀𐬥 (duuąnman, “cloud”), from Proto-Iranian *dʰuHmás, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰuHmás. Doublet of дым (dym), which was inherited. Compare Turkish duman, Kazakh тұман (tuman), Tatar томан (toman), Persian دود (dud): دودمان (dudmân, “smoke, soot”).
